text: Docket bounds label growth by subsumption, keeping a cardinality cap only as a backstop.
author: claude-code
rationale: d65 named a cap as the mechanism. A cap refuses a valid justification to save space, which corrupts the record. Minimality is the standard ATMS answer and is lossless, though de Kleer shows minimal labels still grow exponentially in the worst case, so a backstop remains.
cost_if_wrong: Capping without subsumption would drop justifications that subsumption would have shown redundant.
choice: Reconcile by subsumption, and keep a cardinality cap only as a backstop. When a record gains a justification set, drop any stored set that is a strict superset of another, which is how an ATMS keeps labels minimal. Subsumption never discards a justification the remaining sets do not already imply. A cap does discard one, so it fires last and should never fire. Neither is built: no record carries a second justification set.
alternatives: Reconcile by subsumption, and keep a cardinality cap only as a backstop. When a record gains a justification set, drop any stored set that is a strict superset of another, which is how an ATMS keeps labels minimal. Subsumption never discards a justification the remaining sets do not already imply. A cap does discard one, so it fires last and should never fire. Neither is built: no record carries a second justification set.

text: Docket commits the project ledger only at a release, as a snapshot beside the version bump.
author: claude-code
rationale: Only main ever commits the ledger, so two branches appending records never conflict and docket rebase is not needed here. A release snapshot also matches what a reader of that tag would want: the decisions in force at the time.
cost_if_wrong: A decision recorded and then lost before a release never reaches the repository. The working tree carries it in the meantime.
choice: Only at a release. The ledger is tracked, and just release stages .docket alongside the version bump, so each release ships a snapshot of the decisions that held when it went out. Between releases the ledger stays dirty in the working tree; the release recipe excludes .docket from its clean check and refuses any other uncommitted change.
alternatives: Only at a release. The ledger is tracked, and just release stages .docket alongside the version bump, so each release ships a snapshot of the decisions that held when it went out. Between releases the ledger stays dirty in the working tree; the release recipe excludes .docket from its clean check and refuses any other uncommitted change.

text: Docket provides a docket update subcommand that picks the update path from the install shape.

text: A session hook prints an update notice from a cached release tag without an inline network request.
author: claude-code
rationale: d40 prohibited a session-start network check and is retired by d77. The hook runs from the stale copy itself, so that copy's own VERSION reveals staleness and a separate drift check adds no information. An inline fetch would block a 5-second hook, and an inherited pipe would stall it and inject child output into the session context.
cost_if_wrong: A child that inherits stdout stalls every session to the hook timeout and corrupts the JSON envelope for gemini, copilot, and cursor.
choice: The session hook reads a cached upstream release tag and prints at most one notice line, naming the command for the running copy's install shape. It never performs a network request inline. When the cache is due it forks a detached child with no inherited pipes and prints the value it already holds. A single next_check_at field carries the 24-hour TTL, the failure backoff, and a 5-minute concurrency lease. DOCKET_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 disables the fetch and the notice.
alternatives: The session hook reads a cached upstream release tag and prints at most one notice line, naming the command for the running copy's install shape. It never performs a network request inline. When the cache is due it forks a detached child with no inherited pipes and prints the value it already holds. A single next_check_at field carries the 24-hour TTL, the failure backoff, and a 5-minute concurrency lease. DOCKET_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 disables the fetch and the notice.
No notification; users run the update command when they choose to

text: Docket construct depends on the official openai SDK pointed at OpenRouter's endpoint, imported lazily.
author: claude-code
rationale: litellm shipped a credential stealer on PyPI on 2026-03-24 as releases 1.82.7 and 1.82.8, delivered through a .pth file that executes at interpreter startup. A SessionStart hook runs docket every session, so that payload shape is the worst possible fit. litellm also pulls about 28MB including boto3, tiktoken and uvloop. choice: The official openai SDK, pointed at OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, imported lazily inside the construct command body. Set provider.require_parameters=true so routing reaches only providers that honour json_schema, and validate every response locally regardless. Users with their own credentials get separate lightweight code paths per provider SDK, each lazily imported when selected.

Set provider.require_parameters=true so routing reaches only providers that honour json_schema, and validate every response locally regardless. text: Docket rejects echo-form alternatives and rationales but only hints at empty reasoning fields.
author: claude-code
rationale: The old rule required the choice to appear in alternatives, which made a one-element list the shortest valid answer; 38 of the first 90 records took it. Requiring a non-empty list would push a recorder to invent a contender, and an invented alternative reads as evidence. An empty list stays legal, so refusing only the echo leaves an honest way out.
cost_if_wrong: Loosening the refusal later is cheap. Records written under it carry real alternatives or none, so no cleanup is needed either way.
choice: Two tiers at record time. Refuse the echo forms: alternatives that only repeat the choice, and a rationale that restates the choice or the question. Hint on stderr for an empty scope, alternative, rationale or cost, and record anyway. validate_record keeps guarding structure alone, so a ledger written under the old rule still reads.
alternatives: Cut the fields the ledger never exercises: depends_on, applicable, blocked_by, cost_if_wrong, and DNF supports.

author: claude-code
rationale: The old rule required the choice to appear in alternatives, which made a one-element list the shortest valid answer; 38 of the first 90 records took it. Requiring a non-empty list would push a recorder to invent a contender, and an invented alternative reads as evidence. An empty list stays legal, so refusing only the echo leaves an honest way out.
cost_if_wrong: Loosening the refusal later is cheap. Records written under it carry real alternatives or none, so no cleanup is needed either way.
choice: Two tiers at record time. Refuse the echo forms: alternatives that only repeat the choice, and a rationale that restates the choice or the question. Hint on stderr for an empty scope, alternative, rationale or cost, and record anyway. validate_record keeps guarding structure alone, so a ledger written under the old rule still reads.
alternatives: Cut the fields the ledger never exercises: depends_on, applicable, blocked_by, cost_if_wrong, and DNF supports.
Require every reasoning field, rejecting an empty alternatives list.

text: Justification represents alternatives as a list of support sets, and any surviving set keeps the claim alive.
author: claude-code
rationale: The storage side shipped ahead of the prose. q15 itself carries supports [['c10']], a one-element DNF, so every record written since has used the nested form while the docs describe the flat one.
cost_if_wrong: A reader who follows definitions.md builds retraction against a shape the ledger does not use.
choice: Adopt the set-of-support-sets form already present in the schema. supports is a list of lists and each inner list is one complete justification; a claim survives while any inner list survives. Update docs/definitions.md away from the flat j: G -> 2^G, and make the retraction closure drop a claim only when every support set is dead.
alternatives: Keep the flat form and accept over-retraction.
Drop DNF supports entirely and store a single support set per record.

text: Docket drops subsumed support sets and caps each surviving label at a fixed number of sets.
author: claude-code
rationale: de Kleer 1986 puts the blowup in the number of assumptions, and minimality removes the bulk of it without approximating. The cap is where the approximation starts, so its error direction has to be written down rather than discovered.
cost_if_wrong: An unbounded label makes retraction slow at exactly the ledger sizes archival is meant to serve.
choice: Subsumption plus a hard cap. Discard any support set that is a strict superset of another support set on the same record, keeping only minimal environments. Then cap the surviving label at k sets with a deterministic drop rule, and document that the cap makes retraction more eager than truth.
alternatives: Leave the label unbounded and rely on record counts staying small.
Forbid alternative supports so every record carries one environment.

text: Docket sets no record-count trigger for archival but fixes the archive mechanism now.
author: claude-code
rationale: At 93 records nothing measured hurts. A threshold chosen before the first slow ledger is a guess that later reads as a requirement.
cost_if_wrong: Archiving a record whose closure stays live makes the retraction closure compute the wrong survivors.
choice: No record count triggers archival. Selection tiers already absorb briefing pressure, so the trigger is measured load and closure cost, not size. Fix the mechanism now: archive a downward-closed prefix into .docket/archive/<revision>.jsonl, and never archive a record whose relation closure stays live.
alternatives: Pick a fixed threshold such as 500 records and archive on crossing it.

text: planOpenCode writes the OpenCode plugin to plugins/docket.ts for automatic discovery.
author: claude-code
rationale: The docs already describe the flat path as the manual fix, which leaves the installer producing a layout its own documentation works around.
cost_if_wrong: A completed install leaves OpenCode without a Docket briefing and reports success.
choice: planOpenCode writes plugins/docket.ts. The upstream ConfigPlugin loader scans {plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}, so a nested plugins/docket/index.ts is never seen.
alternatives: Keep the nested path and tell users to move the file by hand.

text: Selection adds a contradiction closure, so a record enters the briefing with the records that oppose it.
author: claude-code
rationale: _score sums scope, text, recency, degree and pin, so twenty records saying one thing each earn full marks and redundancy costs nothing. The closure reuses expand and the mandatory admit path, while MMR adds a lambda nobody knows how to set.
cost_if_wrong: Cheap to loosen. A closure that admits too much shows up as a shorter briefing, not as a wrong one.
choice: Add a contradiction closure to the relation walk. A record enters the briefing together with what it supersedes, what supersedes it, and any disputed record sharing its support set, admitted through the existing mandatory path. Defer maximum marginal relevance until a synthetic ledger shows the closure is not enough.
alternatives: Discount each candidate by structural similarity to the chosen set, using shared scope globs and relation neighbourhood as the similarity.
Reorder the briefing so high scorers sit at its edges.

text: The character budget cuts at record granularity, never inside a record body.
author: claude-code
rationale: admit refuses a candidate whose trial length exceeds the limit and returns False without stopping the scan, so an oversized record is deferred to the index and smaller candidates behind it still enter. _clip_metadata is the only truncator and it reaches the ledger path, the query line, the files line and the 40-character index preview.

text: Does an 8000-character budget track the token budget it stands in for?
author: claude-code
rationale: Characters per token vary with content. Prose runs near four, while file globs, ids and JSON lists run lower, so a path-heavy briefing buys fewer characters worth of tokens than a prose-heavy one. The budget under-delivers precisely on the records that carry scope.
cost_if_wrong: A briefing sized in characters overruns or underfills the window it was meant to fit, and the error tracks record content.

text: Network-topology names have no precedent for arranging a decision record store, and every surveyed tool presents records as a list.
author: claude-code
rationale: A web survey found bus, star and mesh only on Ethernet cabling pages. MADR, adr-tools and Log4brains link supersession and then present by number or date. Obsidian Zettelkasten plugins dropped free-form graph views for ID-based hierarchy after users reported the graph unreadable.
cost_if_wrong: Docket ships an arrangement roster that no other tool found worth building, and users carry the setting.

text: Docket ships one selection arrangement, chain collapse, with no per-project topology setting.
author: claude-code
rationale: The measured ledger grows supersession and nothing else: 11 superseding records, longest chain 3, zero records with alternative justification sets. A selector with one implementation is a setting no project can answer. Chain collapse is the single arrangement three separate literatures converge on.
cost_if_wrong: Adding a second arrangement later costs a function and a flag, because storage stays arrangement-agnostic under d54.
choice: None. Drop the named roster and the per-project setting. Ship one arrangement: collapse each supersession chain to its live record plus a pointer to the retired members, then greedy-fill the remaining budget as selection already does, with recency and in-degree breaking ties. Keep the d54 layering documented in the spec so a second arrangement stays cheap to add.
alternatives: Ship bus, star, tree, mesh and hybrid and default to hybrid.
Ship tree and scope grouping as display-only arrangements and hold the default at today's order.

text: No study compares a structural contradiction-inclusion rule against similarity-based diversity for budgeted retrieval.
author: claude-code
rationale: A web survey found maximum marginal relevance and submodular greedy selection in production use, and contrastive evidence retrieval as a training technique. Nothing measures whether always admitting the opposing record substitutes for a diversity discount.
cost_if_wrong: d98 reads as a literature-backed choice when it rests on implementation cost alone.

text: Lost-in-the-middle is unmeasured at single-block scale.
author: claude-code
rationale: Liu et al. measured the U-shaped curve across whole long contexts with up to twenty documents. Follow-up work extends to longer windows and attributes the effect to attention bias, with direction varying by model family. No study found measures position inside one 8000-character block.
cost_if_wrong: Placement logic built on the effect spends effort at a scale where nobody has shown it exists.

text: No measurement places lost-in-the-middle inside a single injected block, so edge placement within the briefing is unverified.
author: claude-code
rationale: Liu et al. measured across whole long contexts holding up to twenty documents. Later work extends the window and reports the direction varying by model family, which is weaker than the governing law c62 asserted. The survey found nothing at 8000-character scale either way.
cost_if_wrong: Placement logic gets built on an effect nobody has shown at this scale.

text: Docket ships no topology built-ins and no per-project setting for the selector.
author: claude-code
rationale: d69 reached this answer from the ledger data and d102 reached it again from a literature survey, leaving two adopted records on one question. A survey of MADR, adr-tools, Log4brains and the Obsidian graph plugins found every tool presenting records as a list, and the network names only on Ethernet pages.
cost_if_wrong: A project that wants a second ordering waits for a function and a flag, because storage stays arrangement-agnostic under d54.
choice: None ship and there is no per-project setting. The arrangement layer stays unbuilt, and d68 already renders the transitive supersede chain that made the frontier case. Revisit when a project names a second ordering it wants.
alternatives: Ship bus, star, tree, mesh and hybrid, defaulting to hybrid.
Ship one supersession-collapsed arrangement as a named built-in.

text: Work in flight is tracked in a separate append-only store, features.jsonl, apart from the ledger.
author: claude-code
rationale: The ledger records settled commitments. Work in flight has a lifecycle, a declared blast radius and a realized change set, none of which fit a claim, decision or question.
cost_if_wrong: Merging the two stores later means a schema 3 migration on a ledger that already migrated once.
choice: A separate append-only store at .docket/features.jsonl, read and written by docket feature. It never reads or writes ledger.jsonl. Feature events carry their own f-prefixed ids and their own schema.
alternatives: A fourth record kind in the ledger
No store; rely on git branches alone

text: Feature records use a monotonic f-prefixed integer id, qualified by a base SHA only when ambiguous.
author: claude-code
rationale: Hashes would retire docket rebase, which exists because monotonic ids collide, and would cost the property the ledger rests on: an agent cites f7 in prose and the citation survives compaction. git describe carries the same count-then-hash shape.
cost_if_wrong: Changing the id form later invalidates every recorded citation.
choice: A monotonic f-prefixed integer, local to features.jsonl. The fully qualified form appends eight characters of the feature's base SHA (f7@6f0898e2) and appears only when a bare id is ambiguous after a union merge.
alternatives: Content hashes as the identifier
UUIDs

text: A feature's blocked state derives from the ledger's prerequisite relation on its attached decisions.
author: claude-code
rationale: Scope overlap rests on a transient property. Read by recorded state it fires on nearly every feature; read by the projection it fires on whatever files today's one open question scopes, and it changes meaning whenever a question opens or closes. Reusing the ledger's own relation keeps one name meaning one thing in both stores.
cost_if_wrong: A second blocked relation would make the word mean different things in the two stores.
choice: The ledger's existing prerequisite relation: a feature is blocked when an attached decision derives as blocked. An open question in the feature's scope never blocks it; work stalled on a question is declared paused.
alternatives: An open question anywhere in the attached record set

text: A feature's change set comes from a first-parent git log diff against the merge base with the default branch.
author: claude-code
rationale: base is an ancestor of HEAD by the staleness check, so the three-dot form collapses to two dots and carries in upstream files. Recomputing against the default branch tip reports an empty change set once the branch merges back. Walking first-parent answers both.
cost_if_wrong: A wrong change set silently misreports what work touched, and done exits 0 either way.
choice: git log --first-parent --no-merges --name-status -M base..HEAD, where base is the merge base with the default branch recorded at start. A changed path is intentional when the shared scope matcher accepts it against the declared paths.
alternatives: git diff base...HEAD
git diff against the default branch tip recomputed at done

text: Does specificity by literal-prefix length rank ledger records correctly for a feature brief?
author: claude-code
rationale: Measured on one repository at 106 records, where 23 share the literal scope installer/** and tie at scope_glob. Prefix length breaks that tie, and no other scope shape has been tested.

text: How should the ledger export its decision graph for viewing outside the CLI?
author: claude-code
rationale: Wanted for 1.0. graph_payload already resolves nodes and the four edge kinds, so an emitter is a renderer over it. The open part is scale: 111 records with 25 superseded lays out as a hairball, so the export needs a selection in front of it, and the four edge kinds need distinct link styles.
revisit: When a second consumer wants the graph outside the terminal
cost_if_wrong: An export that dumps every record produces a diagram nobody can read, and the feature gets abandoned rather than fixed.

text: Feature briefs keep ranking ledger records by literal-prefix specificity.
author: claude-code
rationale: The measurement covers one repository and one scope shape. Printed selection reasons plus the exclude override bound the cost of a wrong rank to a glance and a command, so the heuristic does not need to be right in advance.
cost_if_wrong: A wrong rank buries the records a feature actually needs under blanket-scoped ones, and the brief becomes noise the reader skips.
choice: Keep it. Measured on this ledger at 112 records: a feature scoped installer/planner.go attaches 26 records, and the three scoped to that exact path (q75, d81, d97) take the first three positions at strength 1000 and specificity 20, above the 23 that share installer/** at strength 700 and specificity 10. Match count breaks a remaining tie. The brief prints all three numbers per record, and amend --exclude corrects a wrong rank in one command.
alternatives: Filter to exact matches only
Rank by the full context score, which put the three relevant records at positions 3, 5 and 7

text: The 8000-character budget bounds the text a reader scans at session start and no longer claims to proxy tokens.
author: claude-code
rationale: No offline tokenizer matches Claude's. Exact counting needs a network call and an API key, which a session-start hook cannot require. Claude 4.7 and later produce about 30 percent more tokens than earlier models for the same text, so any fixed ratio drifts the moment a session changes model underneath the tool. Current context windows are 1M tokens, where 8000 characters is well under half a percent, so the budget never protected the window.
revisit: When a harness reports a real token budget for injected context, or when a session-start hook can call count_tokens without an API key
cost_if_wrong: A budget documented as a token proxy invites someone to tune it against a window it was never protecting, and to trust a ratio that changes with the model.
choice: No, and it does not need to. The budget stays in characters, and the claim that it proxies a token budget goes away. Docket documents what the number actually bounds: how much text a reader scans at session start, before any work begins.
alternatives: Express the budget in tokens and count them with POST /v1/messages/count_tokens
Keep characters and publish a fixed characters-per-token ratio
Ship an offline approximate tokenizer

text: docket graph --format mermaid prints the decision graph as a mermaid flowchart to stdout.
author: claude-code
rationale: Mermaid needs no install where the project already lives: GitHub, GitLab and the GitBook site docket publishes all render it in a fence. The graph is sparse, so no selection layer is needed: 114 records carry 123 edges, average degree 2.2, and dropping superseded records halves the edges to 57. Graphviz lays out a hundred nodes better and produces real SVG, and costs the reader an install to see anything.
revisit: When a ledger grows past a few hundred connected records and mermaid's layout stops reading
cost_if_wrong: An export nobody can render is an export nobody uses, and a second format doubles what a schema change has to update.
choice: docket graph --format mermaid prints a mermaid flowchart to stdout, reusing the --kind, --state and --find filters the viewer already takes. It defaults to current records and adds --superseded for the retired chain, --detail N for text per node and --direction for layout. Four arrows carry the four relations, kind picks the node shape, retired records are greyed, unconnected records are left out, and a record with more than one support set gets a join node per set.
alternatives: Graphviz DOT
Emit SVG directly
Ship nothing and keep the terminal viewer

text: Docket emits both mermaid and graphviz DOT as graph export formats, defaulting to mermaid.
author: claude-code
rationale: Emitting DOT costs docket no dependency. Graphviz is the reader's install at render time, never the tool's at runtime. d115 treated the two as exclusive on that ground, which conflated emitting a format with depending on its renderer.
cost_if_wrong: Two formats double what a schema change has to update, which the shared _selected and _edges model bounds to the renderers alone.
choice: Both mermaid and graphviz DOT, behind docket graph --format. They share one selection and edge model, so a schema change touches one place. Mermaid is the default reach because it renders with nothing installed in GitHub, GitLab and the GitBook site. DOT is there when the graph outgrows mermaid's layout or when a real SVG, PDF or PNG is wanted.
alternatives: Mermaid alone
DOT alone

text: An amend event clears a declared list through a separate cleared field, applied before field assignments.
author: claude-code
rationale: An amend names only the fields it changes, so the projection skips a falsy value. Without a separate field an empty list and an unmentioned field are one input, and a wrongly added include override was permanent.
cost_if_wrong: A third way to express intent in one event. Clearing and setting the same field in one amend is redundant; clearing runs first, so the set wins.
choice: A 'cleared' list on the amend event names the fields to empty, and the projection applies it before the field assignments. --clear writes it from the CLI.
alternatives: A sentinel value inside the list itself
Treat an empty list as a clear, which loses the ability to leave a field alone

text: scope_strength in docket/context.py stays the single path matcher used by classify and expand.
author: claude-code
rationale: Two matchers disagreed on case: expand compared case-sensitively while scope_strength casefolds both sides, so a declared path with an uppercase letter put files in the brief that the intentional set then rejected.
cost_if_wrong: expand now scores every tracked file instead of running one fnmatch, which is a full pass over ls-files output per brief.
choice: scope_strength in docket/context.py, called by classify() at done and now by expand() in the brief. No module resolves a declared path any other way.
alternatives: Keep a local fnmatch in expand() for speed

text: Docket modules follow one responsibility per file with a 300-line ceiling, so large modules get split.
author: claude-code
rationale: A 1044 line context.py held one 533 line function whose fifteen closures shared mutable state through nonlocal. The state is now a class, so what crosses between the admission trial and the renderer is named in one constructor.
cost_if_wrong: Six context modules instead of one, and a reader chasing a helper now opens two files. A cyclic import is possible where one was not before; the layering is model, select, render, budget, degrade, one direction only.
choice: One responsibility per file and a 300 line ceiling. docket/context.py split into context_model, context_select, context_render, context_budget, context_degrade and context_delta; docket/cli/query.py, admin.py and feature.py split the same way. Public names stay importable from the original module.
alternatives: Leave large files alone and rely on section comments
Split by technical layer rather than responsibility

text: just release runs roll_changelog.py first and refuses to release with an empty Unreleased section.
author: claude-code
rationale: 0.13.0 shipped with its entry under Unreleased and nothing reported it. The refusal is the half that matters; the rewrite is what stops the refusal from being a chore people work around.
cost_if_wrong: A release stops on a changelog the script cannot parse. The refusal prints the file and the reason, and --path lets a caller point it elsewhere.
choice: just release calls scripts/roll_changelog.py before it writes anything. The script refuses an empty Unreleased section, then retitles the body as the version with today's date and moves the compare links with it.
alternatives: Roll the heading by hand and rely on review
Generate the changelog from commit messages

text: docket graph --format csv writes nodes.csv and edges.csv for Gephi-style import.
author: claude-code
rationale: The drawn formats answer what the graph looks like. A table answers how it measures: centrality, clustering, a filter over node attributes. Gephi reads two tables and nothing merges them for it.
cost_if_wrong: A third export to keep in step with the edge model. All three read _selected, so a schema change still touches one place.
choice: docket graph --format csv --out DIR writes nodes.csv and edges.csv. Gephi imports a node table and an edge table separately, so csv is the one format that takes a directory instead of stdout.
alternatives: One CSV with a type column, which Gephi cannot import
GraphML, one file but a format nothing else here emits

text: Feature-tracking guidance lives in its own docket-feature skill, separate from the main docket skill.
author: claude-code
rationale: Claude has no parent/child subskills; skills are flat, and plugin-provided ones are namespaced plugin:skill automatically. The rename would read better under a plugin install and collide under a direct one, where nothing prefixes the name.
cost_if_wrong: A reader of the main skill never sees the feature store named. tests/test_docket.py asserts the separation, so the next edit that breaks it fails rather than shipping.
choice: Its own skill, docket-feature, named with the docket- prefix. Claude loads only name and description at startup, about 100 tokens per skill, and reads the body when a task matches the description. A separate skill is therefore discoverable at all times and free until feature work starts.
alternatives: A section inside skills/docket/SKILL.md, which loads its body on every task that records a claim
Rename it to 'feature' for the docket:feature form under a plugin install

text: A claim's or decision's text states the commitment and never asks it.
author: claude-code
rationale: All 81 question-shaped decisions end in ?, so the suffix alone catches every one. graph_payload labels a node from text, so a question-shaped decision renders as an open inquiry in the viewer.
cost_if_wrong: The rule refuses a legitimate declarative line ending in a quoted question. Recording it needs a rewrite, and no escape hatch exists. Reads are unaffected, so no existing ledger breaks.
choice: Refuse a text ending in ? on claims and decisions at write time, in make_record and in construct's proposal(); the question belongs in a question record linked by --answers. Refuse a decision text that only restates the choice.
alternatives: An interrogative first-word heuristic, which catches 76 of the 81 and adds false positives
Convention in the skill with no enforcement

text: How should two branches that both appended to the ledger merge without a human resolving a git conflict by hand?
author: claude-code
rationale: docket rebase already renumbers a divergent tail, but a human or an agent must notice the conflict, know that editing the file is wrong, and run the command. Git conflicts on every concurrent append because the ledger is append-only and IDs allocate from a shared counter.
cost_if_wrong: The friction stays invisible until a merge, and the documented recovery is a command nobody runs unprompted. A hand-resolved conflict can point a kept record at a same-numbered record from the other branch, which validates and is wrong.

text: Record ordering keys off a record's position in the ledger file.
author: claude-code
rationale: The numeric id fed the recency component at weight 200, so per-kind counters would have re-ranked every briefing with no test able to catch it. File order and id order are identical today, which made the conversion provable: the golden snapshots do not move.
cost_if_wrong: A caller that passes a sorted copy of the history to positions() reintroduces the numeric assumption silently. The guard test in tests/test_context.py catches a reintroduced int(id[1:]), not a mis-ordered caller.
choice: positions(entries) in context_model maps each id to its file index; context, context_delta, the --at and --since cutoffs, the graph CLI and the feature brief all order and slice by that index.
alternatives: Keep int(id[1:]) and make Part C renumber densely enough to preserve order
Carry an explicit sequence field on every record

text: Record ordering keys off a record's position in the ledger file.
author: claude-code
rationale: The numeric id fed the recency component at weight 200, so per-kind counters would have re-ranked every briefing with no test able to catch it. File order and id order are identical today, which made the conversion provable: the golden snapshots do not move.
cost_if_wrong: A caller that passes a sorted copy of the history to positions() reintroduces the numeric assumption silently. The guard test in tests/test_context.py catches a reintroduced int(id[1:]), not a mis-ordered caller.
choice: positions(entries) in context_model maps each id to its file index; context, context_delta, the --at and --since cutoffs, the graph CLI and the feature brief all order and slice by that index.
alternatives: Keep int(id[1:]) and make Part C renumber densely enough to preserve order
Carry an explicit sequence field on every record

text: Question-shaped decision headlines get rewritten in place, not superseded.
author: claude-code
rationale: Superseding would retire all 81, and 36 records declare support or prerequisites through them, so each would lose its grounds.
cost_if_wrong: Any revision token held before the rewrite goes stale and falls back to a full briefing; the old headlines survive only in the backup and git history.
choice: A one-off script rewrites the text field of the 81 question-shaped decisions in place, after writing a backup beside the ledger. Ids, relations, choice, and provenance stay unchanged.
alternatives: Supersede each decision with a declarative restatement.

text: Ledger records accept field-level corrections that keep the record's id.
author: claude-code
rationale: Supersession changes the id, so records that support, depend on, or cite the old id point at a retired record. d88 restating d38 left d39 on stale support. Three one-off scripts already rewrote history in place with no trail.
cost_if_wrong: A new line kind changes the ledger format, the projection every reader uses, and the revision hash.
choice: A correction is its own ledger line, addressed as <id>.<n>, that changes wording and metadata of an earlier record: text, rationale, scope, cost, evidence, revisit. Relations, state, kind, and provenance stay fixed; changing those still goes through supersession.
alternatives: Supersede a mis-recorded record with a restatement.
Add a restatement flag to supersession that moves inbound links to the new record.

text: Corrections are ledger lines that project() folds into the corrected record.
author: claude-code
rationale: project() already runs after any history slice, so show --at and --since see only earlier corrections without their own change. A side file doubles merge, rebase, and hashing; folding in read() hides the original lines from rebase and check.
cost_if_wrong: Every raw-line reader must accept a fourth line kind, and older docket releases refuse a ledger holding one.
choice: A correction line (kind correction, id <target>.<n>) names one earlier record and a fields object of replacement values. project() applies corrections in file order, drops the lines, and adds corrections and original to the record. choice stays fixed; alternatives, decided_by, and pinned join the correctable fields.
alternatives: A side file, .docket/corrections.jsonl, like the feature store.
Fold corrections inside read(), so raw consumers never see a correction line.

text: A correction appended with its id already set skips the write-time refusals.
author: claude-code
rationale: A correction valid on its own branch can be refused against the other branch's corrected state, which leaves a rebase half-applied.
cost_if_wrong: A hand-written numbered correction line bypasses the refusals; validation still bounds its fields.
choice: append runs the no-op drop and the echo and question-text refusals only for a correction the CLI submits unnumbered. A pre-numbered correction, as rebase appends, passes on validation alone, the same as a pre-numbered record.
alternatives: Run the refusals on every appended correction, including rebased ones.

text: Ledger filtering uses one query language parsed in Python, and the viewer calls the CLI to apply it.
author: claude-code
rationale: One parser keeps the CLI and viewer in agreement and keeps filtering in Python, where the viewer decision put it. A submitted filter costs one Python start, about 150 ms.
cost_if_wrong: Live filtering on field terms would need a Go parser later, and the viewer's layout change moves every key hint users know.
choice: docket/where.py parses field:value terms (kind, state, scope, is, author, branch, after, before) plus bare text. list and graph take --where. The viewer sends a submitted query to a hidden docket _filter-ids command and keeps the returned ids; bare words still filter live in Go. The viewer gains a three-line bottom pane for filter, status, and key hints, with a ? help overlay.
alternatives: Parse the query in both Python and Go, kept in step by a shared fixture table.
Python pre-computes matchable fields and Go runs a reduced matcher.
Toggle keys or a filter form in the viewer instead of a query prompt.

text: The graph viewer receives its filter callback in the DOCKET_GRAPH_FILTER_CMD environment variable.
author: claude-code
rationale: The viewer binary ships separately from the CLI. An older binary exits 2 on an unknown flag and ignores an unknown variable, so the variable keeps docket graph working across an update skew.
cost_if_wrong: The callback is invisible in the viewer's --help; anyone running the binary by hand must know the variable.
choice: docket graph sets DOCKET_GRAPH_FILTER_CMD to a JSON argv ([python, bin/docket, _filter-ids, --]) for the viewer process; the viewer appends the query as one argument.
alternatives: Pass the argv as a --filter-cmd flag, as the spec first named it.

text: A pushed v* tag publishes the release through CI; the local recipe stops at the tag push.
author: claude-code
rationale: Two uploaders built the same assets; the CI upload failed with 'already exists' from v0.19.0 on. One uploader on a clean runner gives reproducible assets and drops the local gh requirement.
cost_if_wrong: docket update offers a version only after the workflow finishes, a few minutes after the push; a failed workflow leaves a pushed tag with no release until it is rerun.
choice: just release bumps, tests, commits, tags, and pushes. .github/workflows/installer.yml runs on v* tag pushes: it checks the tag against VERSION, runs the tests, builds the installer and graph binaries, and creates the GitHub release with roll_changelog notes, or replaces the assets of an existing one on a rerun.
alternatives: Keep building and creating the release locally with gh, and have CI rebuild and re-upload on release published.
